record.oneLiner: A small, frilled ceratopsian of the Late Cretaceous Gobi Desert.
record.description: Protoceratops was a small ceratopsian from the Late Cretaceous of Asia, 2–2.5 m long, with a proportionally large skull, a neck frill and a prominent parrot-like beak — but no true horns. The frill was likely used for display, combat and muscle attachment. It is extremely well known from the Mongolian Gobi.

notableFacts.text: Had a bony neck frill and parrot-like beak, but no true horns.
Its Gobi nests were once wrongly blamed on Oviraptor, thought to be raiding them.
One of the best-known dinosaurs, from hatchling to adult.
